cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ, welcome back! It's so good to see you again.

cues.caption: Last time: fair AI needs many kinds of examples
cues.text: Last time, we learned that AI needs many kinds of examples to be fair. Just like a crayon box, with lots of colours.

cues.caption: Chapter 2 · AI and Privacy
cues.text: Today is chapter two of Smart and Safe With AI. It's all about AI, and privacy.

cues.caption: Pri · va · cy. What does it mean?
cues.text: Privacy. Hmm. What does that mean? And why does it matter when we use AI apps? Let's find out together.

cues.caption: Meet Aarav, stuck on his science homework
cues.text: Meet Aarav. He's nine, he loves cricket, and today, he's stuck on his science homework.

cues.caption: An AI homework helper on Mum's tablet
cues.text: So his mum lets him use a homework helper on her tablet. It's an AI helper. You type a question, and it explains things.

cues.caption: "I'm Aarav Sharma. I live at 12 Lotus Lane…"
cues.text: The helper says, hi! How can I help? And Aarav gets so excited, he types everything. My name is Aarav Sharma. I study at Green Valley School. I live at twelve Lotus Lane.

cues.caption: Does the helper need all that? Think!
cues.text: Wait a second. Is that a good idea? Does a homework helper need all of that? Think about it.

cues.caption: It only needs his question!
cues.text: Nope! To help with science, it only needs one thing. His question. Not his full name, not his school, and definitely not where he lives.

cues.caption: Keeping your things safe = PRIVACY
cues.text: Keeping some things about you safe, and to yourself, has a name. It's called privacy.

cues.caption: Share personal things only with people you trust
cues.text: Privacy means keeping your personal things safe, and only sharing them with people you trust, like your family.

cues.caption: Name · School · Address · Phone · Photos
cues.text: So, what's personal info? It's things about you. Your full name. Your school. Your address. Your phone number. And photos of you, or your home.

cues.caption: Samosa uncle needs your order, not your address
cues.text: Think about buying samosas at the shop near your school. The uncle needs your order. Two samosas, please! Does he need your home address? Of course not!

cues.caption: "Explain how plants make food" → perfect!
cues.text: An AI helper is the same. Type, explain how plants make food. That's perfect! It's a great question, and it shares nothing private.

cues.caption: Apps can save what you type. Think first!
cues.text: And here's something important. What you type or upload into an app can be saved by the app. Once it's sent, you can't always take it back. So think before you type.

cues.caption: Extra-careful info: three kinds
cues.text: Some info needs extra care. Let's look at three kinds.

cues.caption: 1 · Your real full name and your school
cues.text: One. Your real full name, and your school. Together, they tell a stranger exactly who you are, and where to find you.

cues.caption: 2 · Home address and live location
cues.text: Two. Your home address, and your live location. Live location means where you are right now, shown on a map. That's very private!

cues.caption: 3 · Photos of home, house number, school badge
cues.text: Three. Photos of your home. A house number, a street sign, or your school badge can quietly show where you live.

cues.caption: Name + address can lead someone to your home
cues.text: Why so careful? Because your name and address together can lead someone right to your door.

cues.caption: Detective game: Aarav's new cycle photo
cues.text: Let's play detective! Aarav got a new cycle, and he wants to upload this photo to the homework app, just for fun.

cues.caption: What gives away private info? Spot it!
cues.text: Look closely. What in this photo could show where Aarav lives, or where he studies? Pause, and spot them.

cues.caption: House number · Street sign · School badge
cues.text: There's the house number on the gate. The street sign, Lotus Lane. And the school badge on his shirt! Three clues, in one happy photo.

cues.caption: Ask a parent before sharing photos
cues.text: So, what should Aarav do? Ask a parent before sharing any photo with an app. A grown-up can help check that it's safe.

cues.caption: Game: Share or don't share?
cues.text: Quick game! Share, or don't share? Here come six cards.

cues.caption: Which ones are okay to share?
cues.text: Your homework question. A nickname. Your favourite animal. Your home address. Your phone number. Your password. Which ones are okay to share with an app? Think.

cues.caption: Share fun stuff. Keep private stuff private!
cues.text: Your question, a nickname, and your favourite animal? Those are fine. But your address, your phone number, and your password? Keep those private. Not sure? Stop, and ask a grown-up first.

cues.caption: AI helpers can sound super friendly
cues.text: Now, AI helpers can sound really friendly. They say nice things, like, great question! You're so smart!

cues.caption: It's a program, not a secret-keeping friend
cues.text: But remember. An AI helper isn't a person, and it isn't a friend who keeps your secrets. It's a computer program that finds patterns in words.

cues.caption: Friendly doesn't mean safe!
cues.text: So, friendly doesn't mean safe. Even if an app is fun and kind, don't tell it your school name, or where you live.

cues.caption: Settings = switches for what apps can see
cues.text: Here's some good news. Phones and apps have settings. Settings are like switches. They choose what an app can see, and share.

cues.caption: Parents can use settings to limit sharing
cues.text: Your parents can use these switches to limit what an app is allowed to see. That's a big help in keeping you safe.

cues.caption: Which is safer for a kids' game?
cues.text: Here's a puzzle. For a kids' game, which setting is safer? Location, always on? Or location, off? Think.

cues.caption: Location: OFF is safer
cues.text: Location, off! When it's off, the game can't see where you are. And share my contacts, or show my real name to everyone? Those stay off too.

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, it's practice check time, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: A drawing game wants your location. Now what?
cues.text: You open a fun drawing game, and it asks, can I use your live location? What should you do? Pause the video, and think. Or write it on paper.

cues.caption: Say no, and ask a grown-up to check
cues.text: Here's one answer. Say no, and don't allow it. A drawing game doesn't need to know where you are! Then ask a parent, or a grown-up, to check the settings. Super thinking!

cues.caption: AI doesn't need your life story
cues.text: Let's remember. An AI helper doesn't need your life story. Just your question.

cues.caption: Keep name, location, home photos private
cues.text: Keep your full name, your location, and photos of your home private.

cues.caption: Ask a parent before sharing photos
cues.text: Ask a parent before sharing photos with any app.

cues.caption: Settings can limit what's shared
cues.text: And settings can limit what an app sees, and shares.

cues.caption: Chapter 2 done!
cues.text: Chapter two, done! Now you know what to keep private, champ. That's smart, and safe!

cues.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
